facts: The paper is authored by researchers from the University of Oxford, EPFL, and Yale.
The research addresses the challenge of construct validity in large language model benchmarks.
The study investigates the alignment between benchmark design intentions and their actual validity.
The work highlights potential gaps in how large language model performance is assessed and reported.
The study reviews 445 LLM benchmarks.
29 expert reviewers evaluated the construct validity of the benchmarks.
The researchers identified significant patterns that compromise benchmark validity.
The study provides eight key recommendations for developing future LLM benchmarks.
Benchmarks are essential for developing large language models.
The systematic review analyzed 445 articles from leading ML and NLP conferences.
Nearly all benchmarks have weaknesses in defining phenomena, designing tasks, or selecting metrics.
The authors provide an operational checklist addressing critical areas for benchmark development.
Construct validity assesses whether empirical tests measure their intended phenomena.
It includes dimensions such as face validity, content validity, and ecological validity.
Construct validity is important for benchmarking Large Language Models' reasoning abilities.
The interpretation of LLM evaluations is contested regarding the demonstration of intelligence.

This systematic review analyzed 46,114 articles from major machine learning and NLP conferences between 2018-2024. After keyword filtering, 2,189 articles were screened using four inclusion criteria. GPT-4o mini assisted in screening based on the first three criteria, achieving an 84% F1 score. The inter-rater reliability of the codebook was 0.524 Brennan–Prediger Kappa.
A dataset of 445 benchmark articles was reviewed by 29 NLP and machine learning experts.
Only 78.2% of the benchmarks provided explicit definitions.
Exact matching was the predominant scoring metric at 81.3%.
Only 53.4% of articles discussed construct validity.
The document presents eight recommendations for strengthening the construct validity of LLM benchmarks.
Only a small percentage of reviewed benchmarks implement the recommended practices.
The GSM8K benchmark is analyzed to illustrate its strengths and areas for improvement.
The strengths of the GSM8K benchmark include clear definition and representative dataset construction.
